codenet_p02260.template: Given an integer array A, execute selection sort. For i=0..n-1 set best=i, scan j=i..n-1, and replace best by j exactly when {rule}. If best differs from i, swap A[i],A[best] and increment the swap counter.
codenet_p02260.input_output: Input: n, then n integers. Output: final array on one line, then the number of nontrivial swaps. Ties never replace best.
codenet_p02260.invariant_constraints: Array values are signed integers in[-10^9,10^9].

codechef_walk.template: A route has n ordered segments with minimum acceptable integer speeds W_i. Choose speeds V_i>=W_i such that V_i-V_(i+1)>={rule}. Minimize V_1.
codechef_walk.input_output: Input: test count T; each case has n and n positive W values. Output: minimum initial speed per case.

cf_1155_a.template: Reverse exactly one substring of a lowercase string, using distinct endpoints, to obtain a string lexicographically {rule} than the input.
cf_1155_a.input_output: Input: n and length-n string. Output NO if impossible; otherwise YES and any 1-based l,r with l<r that achieve the objective.
cf_1155_a.invariant_constraints: n>=2; characters are lowercase English letters.

cf_339_a.template: Rearrange the summands of a plus-separated expression into {rule} order. Summands are individual digits1,2,3.
cf_339_a.input_output: Input: one expression such as3+1+2, without spaces. Output the reordered expression with plus separators.
cf_339_a.invariant_constraints: Only digits1,2,3 and single separating plus signs are permitted.

cf_433_a.template: Partition all indivisible apples into two groups such that {rule}. Each apple weighs100 or200.
cf_433_a.l3_rule: their total weights and their numbers of apples are both equal
cf_433_a.input_output: Input: n and n weights. Output YES if such a partition exists, otherwise NO.

cf_500_c.template: There are n distinct books of weights w_i. Choose an initial stack ordering; then perform m requested reads. To read a book, lift all books above it, paying their total weight, and move the requested book to the top. {rule} total paid weight over all initial stack orders.
cf_500_c.input_output: Input: n m; n positive weights; m book IDs in1..n. Output the optimal total weight.
cf_500_c.invariant_constraints: n>=2;1<=w_i<=100; every read ID is in1..n.

cf_5_a.template: Maintain an initially empty participant set. +name joins, -name leaves, name:message sends a message. A send delivers its message to {rule}; each delivery contributes the number of message characters to outgoing traffic. Membership commands contribute zero.
cf_5_a.raw_rule: every current participant, including the sender
cf_5_a.l3_rule: every current participant except the sender
cf_5_a.input_output: Input: commands through EOF, one per line. Names are alphanumeric; a sender is present; messages may contain spaces and may be empty. Joins/removals are valid. Output total traffic.
cf_5_a.invariant_constraints: Each command has at most100 ASCII characters. Names are nonempty alphanumeric strings. Messages use only alphanumeric characters and spaces, without leading/trailing spaces.

cf_670_b.template: Robots have distinct identifiers a_1..a_n. Form rounds r=1..n. In round r append identifiers in order {rule}. Return the identifier at 1-based position k in the concatenation.
cf_670_b.input_output: Input: n k and n identifiers; k lies within the finite concatenation. Output one identifier.

cf_691_d.template: Given a permutation and m allowed pairs of positions, swap either allowed pair any number of times. Find the lexicographically {rule} reachable permutation.
cf_691_d.input_output: Input: n m; permutation1..n; m pairs of1-based positions. Output the resulting permutation.
cf_691_d.invariant_constraints: m>=1; the array is a permutation of1..n; edge endpoints are1-based. Self-loops/repeated edges are permitted.

cf_977_b.template: Count all overlapping length-two substrings of an uppercase string. Return an occurring two-gram with {rule} occurrence count.
cf_977_b.input_output: Input: n and length-n uppercase string, n>=2. Output any optimal two-gram; absent two-grams are ineligible.
cf_977_b.invariant_constraints: n>=2; characters are uppercase English letters.

hackerearth_the_competitive_class_3.template: For every student i define rank_i as one plus the number of students whose mark is strictly {rule} than mark_i. Equal marks receive equal ranks.
hackerearth_the_competitive_class_3.input_output: Input: n then n marks in1..1000. Output the n ranks in input order.

hackerearth_xenny_range_sums.template: For each queried inclusive interval[L,R], report its arithmetic sum and the subtraction fold {rule}. A single-element fold equals that element.
hackerearth_xenny_range_sums.input_output: Input: n q; n signed integers; q pairs1<=L<=R<=n. Output sum and fold on one line per query.

atcoder_abc154_e.template: Count positive integers x<=N whose decimal representation contains {rule} K nonzero digits. Zero is excluded.
atcoder_abc154_e.input_output: Input: positive decimal N and K in1..3. Output the exact integer count without a modulus.
atcoder_abc154_e.invariant_constraints: N>=1,1<=K<=3, and N has no leading zero.

atcoder_abc140_b.template: Eat all n dishes in the given permutation. Dish i grants base satisfaction B_i; bonus C_i is granted when {rule}. Return total satisfaction.
atcoder_abc140_b.raw_rule: dish i+1 is eaten immediately after dish i
atcoder_abc140_b.l3_rule: dish i is eaten immediately after dish i+1
atcoder_abc140_b.input_output: Input: n; permutation A of1..n; n base values B; n-1 bonus values C. Output total satisfaction.
atcoder_abc140_b.invariant_constraints: n>=2; A is a permutation1..n; every B_i,C_i is in1..50.

hackerearth_new_world_11.template: Stones have strictly increasing integer coordinates. Travel from first to last using exactly K forward jumps between stones. {rule}.
hackerearth_new_world_11.input_output: Input: T; each case n K and n coordinates,1<=K<n. Output the optimum length per case.
hackerearth_new_world_11.invariant_constraints: 1<=K<n; coordinates are distinct increasing integers in1..10^9.

codenet_p02327.template: In a binary rectangular grid, find the largest axis-aligned contiguous rectangle consisting entirely of {rule}.
codenet_p02327.input_output: Input: height width followed by the grid as whitespace-separated bits. Output area, or0 when no qualifying cell exists.

cf_1011_a.template: Choose exactly k letters from n supplied stage instances. In sorted order every adjacent chosen letter must differ by at least two alphabet positions. Letter a has weight1,...,z has weight26. {rule} total chosen weight.
cf_1011_a.input_output: Input: n k then a lowercase string of length n. Output optimum weight, or-1 if impossible.
cf_1011_a.invariant_constraints: 1<=k<=n; stage letters are lowercase English letters; repeated letters are separate instances.

cf_1121_a.template: Every school selects its student with {rule} power. Powers are distinct. Reassign students to newly created schools, paying one per new school, so that every one of the k chosen students is selected. Minimize new schools.
cf_1121_a.input_output: Input: n m k; permutation powers1..n; school IDs of n students; k distinct chosen student IDs. All m schools are initially nonempty. Output minimum required new schools.
cf_1121_a.invariant_constraints: 1<=m,k<=n. Powers are a permutation1..n. All school IDs1..m occur. Chosen student IDs are distinct.

cf_1225_b1.template: Among all contiguous length-d windows of a show sequence, return the {rule} number of distinct show IDs.
cf_1225_b1.input_output: Input: T; each case n k d and n IDs in1..k,1<=d<=n. Output one optimum count per case.

cf_166_a.template: Rank teams by solved count descending, breaking ties by penalty {rule}. Teams with identical pairs share their rank group. Count teams whose pair equals the kth team after sorting.
cf_166_a.input_output: Input: n k and n pairs of solved count and penalty. Output the size of the kth pair group.
cf_166_a.invariant_constraints: 1<=k<=n; solved counts and penalties each lie in1..50.

cf_46_c.template: The characters H and T describe two species in an arrangement interpreted as {rule}. Swap any two positions at unit cost to make the positions of each species one contiguous block. Minimize swaps.
cf_46_c.raw_rule: a circle with adjacent first and last positions
cf_46_c.l3_rule: a fixed line whose first and last positions are not adjacent
cf_46_c.input_output: Input: n and a length-n string containing both H and T. Output minimum swaps.
cf_46_c.invariant_constraints: n>=2; the string contains only H,T and contains both species.

cf_633_a.template: Two guns deal damage a and b per shot. Determine whether total damage c can be obtained with integer shot counts x,y satisfying {rule}.
cf_633_a.input_output: Input: positive a b c. Output Yes if a*x+b*y=c is feasible, otherwise No.

cf_865_d.template: A stock has positive prices on n days. Make at most one buy, sell, or idle action each day; every transaction is one share. Inventory starts and ends at zero and must remain {rule}. Maximize cash profit.
cf_865_d.raw_rule: nonnegative, so selling before owning is forbidden
cf_865_d.l3_rule: nonpositive, so buying is allowed only to cover a short position
cf_865_d.input_output: Input: n and n prices. Output maximum profit; doing nothing is allowed.

atcoder_abc130_e.template: From sequences S and T independently select subsequences by increasing index sets. Count ordered pairs with equal value sequences and {rule}. Distinct index sets count separately.
atcoder_abc130_e.raw_rule: any length, including the empty pair
atcoder_abc130_e.input_output: Input: n m, n integers S, m integers T. Output count modulo1000000007.

atcoder_abc105_d.template: Count nonempty contiguous intervals whose sum modulo M equals {rule}.
atcoder_abc105_d.input_output: Input: n M, with M>=2; n positive integers. Output the interval count.

atcoder_abc171_d.template: For each operation(B,C), simultaneously replace every current occurrence of value B by C. After each operation report the {rule} of all array elements.
atcoder_abc171_d.input_output: Input: n and n positive values; q; q pairs B C with B!=C. Output one aggregate after each replacement.
atcoder_abc171_d.invariant_constraints: Array values and replacement values lie in1..100000; B!=C.

atcoder_dp_m.template: Distribute identical candies among n distinct children. Child i receives an integer in[0,a_i]. Count allocations with total candies distributed {rule} K.
atcoder_dp_m.input_output: Input: n K and n bounds a_i in[0,K]. Output count modulo1000000007. An allocation is determined by all children counts.

cf_1152_a.template: A chest can be unlocked by a key exactly when their two integer labels have {rule} sum. Each chest and each key can be used at most once. Maximize unlocked chests.
cf_1152_a.input_output: Input: n m; n chest labels; m key labels. Output maximum matching size.
cf_1152_a.invariant_constraints: Chest and key labels lie in1..10^9.

cf_1165_e.template: Keep a fixed and permute b. For every interval[l,r], define f(l,r)=sum_(i=l..r)(a_i*b_i). {rule} the integer total over all intervals; take the modulus only after choosing the optimal permutation.
cf_1165_e.input_output: Input: n; n positive a values; n positive b values. Output optimal integer total modulo998244353.

cf_372_a.template: A kangaroo can hide at most one other kangaroo. A hidden kangaroo cannot itself hide another. A holder size must be {rule} twice the held size. Minimize the number visible.
cf_372_a.input_output: Input: n and n positive sizes. Output minimum visible count.

cf_489_b.template: Pair boys with girls with each person used at most once. A pair is valid when {rule}. Maximize pairs.
cf_489_b.raw_rule: their integer skills differ by at most one
cf_489_b.input_output: Input: number of boys and their skills; number of girls and their skills. Output maximum pairs.

cf_1000_c.template: Interval i covers integer x under the predicate {rule}. For each k=1..n count integer coordinates covered by exactly k intervals.
cf_1000_c.input_output: Input: n and n endpoint pairs0<=l_i<=r_i. Output n counts.

cf_1215_b.template: For every nonempty contiguous interval of a nonzero integer array, compute its {rule}. Count negative results and positive results, excluding zero results.
cf_1215_b.input_output: Input: n and n nonzero signed integers. Output negative count then positive count.

cf_740_b.template: Each suggested interval contributes the sum of its array elements. Choose any subset of suggestions; overlapping intervals contribute independently, including repeated elements. {rule} total contribution; choosing no intervals is allowed.
cf_740_b.input_output: Input: n m; n signed values; m inclusive1-based intervals. Output optimum contribution.

cf_451_d.template: For each substring of a binary-alphabet string, {rule} and test whether the result is a palindrome. Count successful substrings by their original length parity.
cf_451_d.raw_rule: merge every maximal run of identical characters into one character
cf_451_d.l3_rule: keep its characters exactly as they are
cf_451_d.input_output: Input: a nonempty string using a,b. Output the count with even original length, then the count with odd original length.

cf_1157_e.template: Permute b arbitrarily and define c_i=(a_i+b_i) modulo n. Output the lexicographically {rule} possible c.
cf_1157_e.input_output: Input: n, n integers a, n integers b, each in0..n-1. Output n residues.

cf_1392_b.template: Perform k simultaneous transformations of an integer array. In each transformation set d to the {rule} of the current array, then replace every a_i by d-a_i.
cf_1392_b.input_output: Input: T; each case n k and n signed integers, k>=1. Output the final array per case.

cf_658_b.template: Friends have distinct friendship values and are initially offline. When a friend comes online they stay online. Display up to k online friends with the {rule} friendship values. Queries ask whether a friend is displayed.
cf_658_b.input_output: Input: n k q; n distinct values; q commands(1,id) to come online once or(2,id) to query. Output YES/NO for each type2. k<=6.
cf_658_b.invariant_constraints: 1<=k<=min(6,n); friendship values are distinct integers in1..10^9. Type1 IDs have not appeared in an earlier type1. At least one type2 query is present.

cf_747_c.template: There are n servers numbered1..n. A task(t,k,d) arrives at integer time t and needs k idle servers for[t,t+d). If fewer than k are idle reject it; otherwise select the k idle servers with {rule} IDs.
cf_747_c.input_output: Input: n q; q triples with strictly increasing t. Output-1 for rejected tasks, otherwise sum of assigned server IDs.
cf_747_c.invariant_constraints: Times are strictly increasing integers in1..10^6;1<=k<=n and1<=d<=1000. A server released at time t is available to a task arriving at t.

cf_90_b.template: Read a lowercase letter grid in row-major order and retain a cell exactly when its letter occurs {rule}. Concatenate the retained letters in that order.
cf_90_b.raw_rule: exactly once in its row and exactly once in its column
cf_90_b.l3_rule: at least twice in its row and at least twice in its column
cf_90_b.input_output: Input: height width and height letter strings. The input has at least one row-and-column-unique letter. Output the retained string; an empty output is allowed.
cf_90_b.invariant_constraints: Letters are lowercase English letters. At least one cell is unique in both its row and its column.

atcoder_abc176_c.template: Raise each integer height by a nonnegative integer amount until the resulting sequence is {rule}. Minimize the sum of all increases.
atcoder_abc176_c.input_output: Input: n and n positive heights. Output minimum total increase.

atcoder_abc147_d.template: Sum A_i {rule} A_j over all i<j.
atcoder_abc147_d.input_output: Input: n>=2 and n integers0<=A_i<2^60. Output the sum modulo1000000007.

atcoder_abc075_b.template: A grid contains bombs(#) and empty cells(.). Replace each empty cell by the number of bombs in its {rule}; preserve every bomb.
atcoder_abc075_b.input_output: Input: height width and the grid. Output transformed grid; cells outside the grid contribute nothing.

codenet_p00451.template: For every pair of uppercase strings, output the length of a longest common {rule}.
codenet_p00451.l3_rule: subsequence, formed by deleting characters without reordering
codenet_p00451.input_output: Input: pairs of whitespace-separated nonempty uppercase strings through EOF. Output one integer for each pair.
codenet_p00451.invariant_constraints: Each string contains only uppercase English letters; the number of strings is even.

cf_215_a.template: A front gear a_i and rear gear b_j are eligible when b_j is divisible by a_i. Count eligible pairs attaining the {rule} integral ratio b_j/a_i.
cf_215_a.input_output: Input: n, increasing distinct positive front sizes; m, increasing distinct positive rear sizes. Every size<=10000 and an eligible pair exists. Output pair count.
cf_215_a.invariant_constraints: Front sizes and rear sizes are separately strictly increasing and lie in1..10000. At least one integral ratio exists.

cf_191_a.template: Choose a nonempty chronological subsequence of names so each name final character equals the next name first character. Additionally require the first and final characters of the whole dynasty to {rule}. Maximize total name length.
cf_191_a.input_output: Input: n and n lowercase names. Output maximum length, or0 if no valid dynasty exists.
cf_191_a.invariant_constraints: Names are lowercase English strings of length1..10.

codechef_cielrcpt.template: There are twelve menu prices1,2,4,...,2048. Order menus totaling exactly p, with each menu price usable {rule}. Minimize the number ordered.
codechef_cielrcpt.input_output: Input: T and T positive amounts p. Output minimum number, or-1 if the exact amount is impossible.

cf_1097_b.template: Starting at angle0 degrees, perform every given rotation in sequence, independently choosing clockwise or counterclockwise direction. Determine whether the final angle modulo360 can be {rule}.
cf_1097_b.input_output: Input: n and n angles in1..180. Output YES if feasible, otherwise NO.

cf_1031_b.template: Find t_1..t_n in0..3 such that a_i=t_i {rule} t_(i+1) and b_i=t_i AND t_(i+1), for every adjacent pair.
cf_1031_b.input_output: Input: n; n-1 values a; n-1 values b. Output NO if impossible; otherwise YES and any valid n-value sequence.
cf_1031_b.invariant_constraints: n>=2; all supplied relation values lie in0..3.

cf_1203_a.template: Students numbered1..n stand in a circle in the given clockwise order. Accept if their order is a cyclic rotation of {rule}.
cf_1203_a.input_output: Input: q; each case n and a permutation1..n. Output YES/NO per case.
cf_1203_a.invariant_constraints: Each circle is a permutation of1..n.

codenet_p02398.template: Among integers d in[a,b] dividing c exactly, output their {rule}.
codenet_p02398.input_output: Input: positive a b c with a<=b. Output one integer.

atcoder_abc128_c.template: There are n binary switches. Bulb i is on exactly when the sum of connected switch states modulo2 equals p_i. Count assignments for which every bulb is {rule}.
atcoder_abc128_c.input_output: Input: n m; each of m lines gives count k_i then distinct1-based connected switch IDs; then m bits p_i. Output exact assignment count.
atcoder_abc128_c.invariant_constraints: Each bulb connects to a nonempty subset of distinct switches1..n; every p_i is0 or1.

codechef_prime1.template: For each inclusive interval[l,r], list all {rule} integers in increasing order. The integer1 belongs to neither class.

codechef_frgtnlng.template: For each dictionary word, answer YES exactly when it occurs in {rule} supplied modern phrases. Multiple occurrences inside one phrase count once.

cf_239_a.template: List all positive integers x with x+y<=n and(x+y) modulo k equal to {rule}.
cf_239_a.input_output: Input: positive y k n. Output all solutions in increasing order, or-1 if absent. When k=1 no number has remainder1.

cf_846_a.template: From a binary sequence delete any entries without reordering the rest. Retain the maximum number such that the retained sequence is {rule}.
cf_846_a.input_output: Input: n and n bits. Output the maximum retained length.

atcoder_abc103_b.template: Determine whether T can be obtained from S by {rule}.

atcoder_abc103_b.input_output: Input: equal-length lowercase strings S and T, length>=2. Output Yes or No.

atcoder_abc087_c.template: Travel in a two-row grid from top-left to bottom-right, moving only right or down. Collect every visited cell value including endpoints. {rule} collected sum.
atcoder_abc087_c.input_output: Input: N; N top-row values; N bottom-row values. All values are positive. Output optimum sum.

cf_1066_a.template: Lanterns occupy positive positions divisible by v on the path1..L. Count visible lanterns when positions satisfying {rule} are blocked.
cf_1066_a.input_output: Input: T; each query L v l r with1<=l<=r<=L. Output visible count per query.

cf_1213_b.template: Day i is bad exactly when a later day has price {rule} a_i. Count bad days.
cf_1213_b.input_output: Input: T; each case n and n positive prices. Output bad-day count per case.

cf_1278_a.template: Determine whether some permutation of password p occurs in h as a {rule}. Every password letter must be used exactly once.
cf_1278_a.input_output: Input: T; each case nonempty lowercase p and h. Output YES or NO per case.
cf_1278_a.invariant_constraints: p,h are nonempty lowercase English strings.

cf_1321_b.template: Choose a nonempty increasing sequence of city indices c_1<...<c_k. For every adjacent selected pair i<j require j-i={rule}. Maximize the sum of selected positive beauty values.
cf_1321_b.input_output: Input: n and n positive beauty values b. Output maximum beauty sum.

cf_1547_e.template: At cell i of a line1..n define temperature as {rule}_j(t_j+abs(a_j-i)) across all air conditioners.
cf_1547_e.input_output: Input: T; each case n k, k distinct positions a, k positive temperatures t. Output all n cell temperatures.
cf_1547_e.invariant_constraints: 1<=k<=n; conditioner positions are distinct and lie in1..n;1<=t_i<=10^9; total n<=300000.

cf_242_e.template: Maintain an integer array with type2 operations(l,r,x) XORing every entry of inclusive[l,r] by x. A type1 query(l,r) returns the {rule} of entries in that range.
cf_242_e.input_output: Input: n; n values in0..10^6; q; q lines1 l r or2 l r x,1<=x<=10^6. Output one answer for each type1 query.

cf_5_c.template: Interpret {rule}. A regular substring has nonnegative balance in every prefix and total balance zero. Find the maximum positive regular substring length and the number of substrings attaining it.
cf_5_c.input_output: Input: a nonempty parenthesis string. Output maximum length and count; if no regular nonempty substring exists output0 1.
cf_5_c.invariant_constraints: Only characters ( and ) are permitted; the string is nonempty.

cf_670_d1.template: A cookie requires a_i grams of each of n ingredients, and current stock is b_i. Powder {rule}. Maximize whole cookies.
cf_670_d1.raw_rule: is a shared budget of k grams, each convertible to any one ingredient
cf_670_d1.l3_rule: provides a separate budget of k grams for each ingredient, with no transfers between these budgets
cf_670_d1.input_output: Input: n k; n positive requirements a; n positive stocks b. Output maximum cookie count.

atcoder_agc009_a.template: Button i {rule} each of the first i entries of A by one. Press buttons until every A_i is an integer multiple of B_i; final multiples may be negative or zero. Minimize total presses.
atcoder_agc009_a.input_output: Input: N followed by N pairs A_i B_i with A_i>=0 and B_i>=1. Output minimum presses.
atcoder_agc009_a.invariant_constraints: A_i>=0,B_i>=1. The applicable profile additionally caps values; final values need not remain nonnegative.

codechef_sumpair.template: Choose disjoint index pairs from a positive integer array. A pair is good when its absolute value difference is {rule} D. Maximize the sum of all elements in chosen good pairs.
codechef_sumpair.input_output: Input: T; each case N D and N positive integers. Output optimum sum; using no pairs is allowed.

cf_1538_c.template: Count index pairs i<j whose sum satisfies {rule}.
cf_1538_c.input_output: Input: T; each case n l r and n positive integers. Output one pair count per case.

hackerearth_roy_coin_boxes.template: Initially all N boxes have zero coins. For each of M inclusive intervals[L,R], add one coin to every covered box. Each query X asks how many boxes have {rule} X coins.
hackerearth_roy_coin_boxes.input_output: Input: N; M; M interval pairs; Q; Q positive query values X. Output one count per query.

atcoder_abc088_b.template: Alice and Bob alternately take one remaining card; Alice starts. Their score is the sum of their chosen card values. Both optimally {rule} their own final score. Return Alice score minus Bob score.
atcoder_abc088_b.input_output: Input: N and N positive card values. Output the score difference under optimal play.

codenet_p02240.template: Given an undirected graph, answer whether each queried pair s,t is connected by {rule}.
codenet_p02240.l3_rule: an even-length walk; revisiting vertices and edges is allowed, and the empty walk has length0
codenet_p02240.input_output: Input: n m; m edges with IDs0..n-1; q; q vertex pairs. Output yes/no per pair.
codenet_p02240.invariant_constraints: n>=2; edge and query endpoints lie in0..n-1. Self-loops/repeated edges are allowed. The empty walk witnesses reachability of a vertex to itself.

cf_302_a.template: For each query[l,r], independently rearrange the entire array of values+1 and-1. Determine whether the sum in positions[l,r] can equal {rule}.
cf_302_a.input_output: Input: n q; n values each+1 or-1; q inclusive1-based intervals. Output1 if feasible, otherwise0, per query.

cf_467_c.template: Choose exactly k pairwise disjoint contiguous intervals of length m. {rule} the total sum of all chosen elements.
cf_467_c.input_output: Input: n m k with m*k<=n; n nonnegative integers. Output optimum total.

cf_705_c.template: Initially there are no notifications. Type1 x appends an unread notification from application x. Type2 x reads all notifications generated so far by application x. Type3 t reads the {rule} t notifications generated so far, including already read notifications.
cf_705_c.input_output: Input: n q; q commands, each type and argument. Each type3 t is no greater than total generated notifications. Output the total unread count after every command.
cf_705_c.invariant_constraints: Application IDs lie in1..n; type3 arguments are positive and no greater than the number of prior type1 events.

cf_911_d.template: For each query[l,r], {rule} the permutation segment. After each operation report whether total inversions is odd or even. An inversion is i<j with a_i>a_j.
cf_911_d.l3_rule: cyclically rotate left by one position

atcoder_agc047_a.template: Count i<j such that the exact decimal product A_i*A_j is {rule}.
